questions.prompt: Which file must every Gemini CLI extension have in its root folder?

options.explanation: Right. Gemini CLI says each extension must have a gemini-extension.json file in its root directory.
That is the Claude Code plugin manifest.
A marketplace file lists plugins. It is not an extension's manifest.

questions.prompt: You uninstall a plugin in ChatGPT or Codex. What happens to its separately connected MCP servers?

options.explanation: The Codex docs say they stay connected in ChatGPT until you disconnect them there.
Right. Disconnect them yourself after you remove the plugin.

options.text: They move to a new plugin
options.explanation: No page says that. They stay connected until you disconnect them.

questions.prompt: You need one skill in one repo, and nothing else. Do you need a plugin?

options.text: Yes, every skill must ship in one
options.explanation: The Claude Code docs say skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers all work on their own, without a plugin.

options.text: No, a skill folder works on its own
options.explanation: Right. A plugin is for packaging several parts as one unit, or sharing them across repos.

options.text: Yes, unless the repo is private
options.explanation: Repo visibility does not decide it. A single skill works without a plugin.
